questions.question: What is the maximum size of a single item in Cosmos DB?
questions.referenceAnswer: A single item in Azure Cosmos DB can be up to 2 MB in size.

questions.question: What happens to messages in Service Bus after the maximum delivery count is exceeded?
questions.referenceAnswer: The message is moved to the dead-letter queue (DLQ), where it can be inspected and reprocessed separately.

questions.question: Does Azure Container Apps support scaling to zero replicas?
questions.referenceAnswer: Yes. Azure Container Apps supports scale-to-zero: with KEDA-based scale rules, an app can scale down to zero replicas when there is no load, and no compute charges accrue while at zero.

questions.question: What two retrieval methods does hybrid search in Azure AI Search combine?
questions.referenceAnswer: Hybrid search combines full-text (BM25 keyword) search and vector similarity search in a single query, merging results with Reciprocal Rank Fusion.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a partition key in Cosmos DB?
questions.referenceAnswer: The partition key determines how items are distributed across physical partitions. Items with the same partition key value are stored in the same logical partition, which scopes transactions and keeps related data co-located for efficient queries.

questions.question: I need a messaging layer for a worker that should scale with queue depth and cost nothing when idle. Which Azure services fit and why?
questions.referenceAnswer: Use Azure Service Bus queues for the messaging layer (competing consumers, retries, dead-lettering) and run the worker on Azure Container Apps with a KEDA scale rule on queue length, which scales the worker out with queue depth and down to zero replicas when the queue is empty.

questions.question: How do availability zones relate to the reliability pillar's guidance on redundancy?
questions.referenceAnswer: The reliability pillar recommends redundancy across fault domains; availability zones provide physically separate datacenters within a region, and zone-redundant deployments keep a workload available when a single zone fails.
